reviews.text:
This is a trustworthy hospital that puts cats first.
They also respond to consultations with sincerity.

Thank you for your continued support.

This is a hospital where I can feel at ease bringing my cats, as they are very considerate of their needs.

The head veterinarian's skills are excellent, and the doctors and staff are all very kind and gentle.

I am truly grateful for the thorough care I always receive.

Thank you for always taking care of my beloved cat.

We have Dr. Fujikura, a female veterinarian, who is kind to both cats and their owners, yet provides accurate and thorough explanations until we fully understand. She puts my anxieties at ease.

She is also very conscientious and clearly has extensively researched and studied cats, which is evident from everything she says.

No matter what I ask, she explains the cat's habits and the underlying reasons. Even though it's a long drive, I consider this the best place to go for anything related to my cat.

We also have our cat undergo a comprehensive health checkup, and while it depends on how busy she is, she tries her best to complete it as quickly as possible to minimize stress on the cat.

She doesn't push expensive or pushy options; instead, she suggests choosing the same checkup as last time, saying that it's better to choose the same one to see the difference.

She also helps us choose optional checkups in consultation with us, which is very helpful, and I trust her completely.


He also calls the cat by name and waves, saying "See you later," so more than anything, the cat loves Professor Fujikura.

Please feel free to contact us again if anything comes up.

Waiting Room Problem
Too many accompanying persons!
I think the doctor and staff are wonderful.
However, I wish they would stop bringing in cats plus two accompanying persons.
No matter how many waiting rooms there are, it's never enough.
I think they should limit the number of accompanying persons.
I went to the clinic because of bloody stools. The pre-examination tests made the consultation go smoothly.

They examined me very carefully 🥰
The next day after the examination, they called me and gave me lots of advice 🥰 …

The doctor is very kind.
I feel relieved knowing they also have consultations on Sundays.

I am receiving treatment for cancer. I have a doctor in charge, but even when my doctor is on leave, the team takes care of me. There are some negative reviews about the reception staff, but they are very knowledgeable, know the taste of kibble, and work efficiently and without waste, so I rely on them. I don't know how much longer I will be able to live with my pet, but I am receiving treatment with their support, as I have not given up on living.
Great! My cat's diarrhea had been repeatedly diagnosed at other hospitals for the past two years, but after just one examination here, the cause was found.

They were open on Sundays, and my male cat was taken care of there. 🐱
However, even though I went there every day, they only gave me first aid... The diagnosis, plan, and instructions were all unclear. 💦 In the end, I went to the emergency room for a second opinion and had to undergo surgery right away. 💦
They were very quick in referring me to the center. 🤲🏻

We are under the care of the associate director.

He always explains things carefully, no matter how many questions I have.

I feel he is a good doctor who works with me to consider what is best for my cat.

If I were to be selfish, it would be helpful if we could see the nail trimming process in front of the owner, so we can learn from it.
The teacher is very kind, and their explanations are clear and thorough. I can trust them completely.

I feel this is a really good hospital.
I think it's because they've seen many different cats and are able to handle a variety of situations. They discuss various possibilities, and their system is well-established.
And the doctor is very caring.
They respond immediately when I'm in trouble.

When my cat was diagnosed with lymphoma, it was my first time dealing with something like this, and I had so many questions, but I was worried because I couldn't set aside time to ask them separately.
I lined up at the reception as usual and went to consult when it was my turn for my appointment, but seeing so many people lined up in the waiting room made me hesitant to ask questions for a long time.
What I realized after starting cancer treatment is that there are many things you can't know until you've actually started treatment, and I now understand that even if I had consulted them at the beginning, I probably wouldn't have received answers that satisfied me. However, when your pet cat gets cancer, it's natural for the owner to be anxious.
It was painful not being able to ask questions freely.

I feel that choosing a hospital is something that the owner must decide with a firm resolve.
I felt that the responsibility lay not with the doctor, but with myself. If I wasn't satisfied, I decided to get a second opinion and switch hospitals, wanting to find a place where I could thoroughly investigate and consult with the doctor completely.

(The doctor who was in charge of my pet also recommended this hospital.)

Incidentally, since it's not appointment-based, you can sometimes wait for over an hour in the middle of summer. It's understandable since it's a popular hospital, and it's trulyありがたい (grateful) that they'll see you right away if you wait a little when you're really in trouble.

Choosing a veterinary hospital is all about compatibility.

My cat was in critical condition due to an acute illness, and you saved her life.

I can't thank you enough.

Thanks to Dr. Oku, I was able to spend my last moments with my beloved cat as peacefully and for as long as possible.
I am truly grateful.
From the initial consultation to the diagnosis and treatment, including coordination, everything was swift and compassionate, allowing me to alleviate one of my regrets about saying goodbye to my cat.
Even though I felt I might be bothering them during clinic hours, they gave me the best advice over the phone.

I was introduced to Dr. Oku by someone who had also lost a cat, and I'm so glad I trusted their recommendation that he provides the best service in the area.
Thank you so much.

I will definitely visit again when I get another cat.

However, I can only imagine the immense physical and mental strain on the doctors. Please take care of yourselves.

After the head veterinarian's examination, I was told that hospitalization wasn't necessary, but my pet died in the car on the way home. When I went back to inquire about the cause, they said, "Sudden death is possible?" If that's the case, shouldn't they have hospitalized my pet? Furthermore, even though I requested a head veterinarian examination, he didn't actually examine my pet. He only gave the explanation. From what I could see through a gap, it was awful. The consultation fee was 80,000 yen.

I didn't feel any sincerity, and they treated the life of a living creature far too carelessly. Living things aren't objects. They're not tools for making money. It's absolutely terrible.

All of my cats are well taken care of.
A cat-only hospital is so reassuring.
Even if your cat doesn't have specific symptoms like diarrhea or vomiting, if you mention that something seems different, they'll find out all the details and investigate. It's so reassuring as a pet owner.

When my cat had lymphoma, they said, "That's a nasty sneeze," and quickly referred me to a secondary care hospital. There, we had an MRI and three pathology tests, and the diagnosis was lymphoma. I think it's impressive that they were able to diagnose something suspicious at such an early stage.

Also, not only Dr. Hattori, but also Dr. Yoshida are very compassionate when examining cats. Even just passing each other in the hallway, they'll ask, "Are you OK, XX?"... It's amazing, considering they have so many patients.

Many people have written that the receptionists are unfriendly, and it's true that they are not very friendly (lol), but they do their job efficiently, respond quickly to phone calls, and when I went in because my kitten was sick, they looked in the carrier and immediately took it to the second floor (examination room). They do what they need to do properly.

It's certainly better to be friendly, but I think they have a wealth of knowledge and experience, so I think their service is quite thorough. They're not just receptionists.

So, all the staff at this hospital are trustworthy, and I can visit with peace of mind. The only downside is that it's often crowded, and the wait times are long.

My family lives just under an hour away by train or car, but I hope to continue using your services in the future.

Thank you for your continued support.
This is a very trustworthy and reassuring hospital 🐈✨ …
Thanks to your accurate diagnosis, my pet was able to pass away peacefully. Thank you very much.

The receptionist was incredibly rude. I was really put off by how she handled things, especially considering it's customer service.

She smiled occasionally, but it was so rare I wondered if it depended on her mood.

The prices seemed a little higher than other places. I also question the practice of prescribing antibiotics while waiting for the results of a feline ringworm culture test, as others have mentioned. Wouldn't it have been less stressful for my cat if they had just taken a light test and given me some topical medication?

However, I suppose other hospitals are the same, which is why I came here, since they advertise themselves as cat specialists.
I was so moved when I read the newspaper 🥰(*^o^)／＼(^-^*) Dr. Hattori, please keep up the great work (^o^)／~~ …

My cat was diagnosed with FIP, and since the hospital we were going to couldn't handle it, we were referred here.

Dr. Hattori was in charge, and he presented us with several treatment options, including the cost of tests and medications, the estimated future costs, and the type of treatment. He patiently waited for us to make a decision.

After three months of medication and visits, our cat was successfully in remission.

We have continued to bring our other cats here for illnesses since then.

Dr. Hattori is a wonderful doctor who is very loving towards cats, and he is very attentive, providing thorough examinations and treatments, so we feel at ease bringing our cats here.

Sometimes we have to wait for almost an hour, but in emergencies they see patients immediately.

The receptionist is incredibly unfriendly, and I'm always disappointed by her attitude, but I put up with it because the doctor is wonderful.
When I inquired by email, they replied the same day despite being busy. It was extremely helpful.

I took my cat in for a cough.

The doctor was very kind and explained everything thoroughly, even discussing the cat's breed and temperament. They also addressed my concerns clearly and patiently.

Specialized tests are popular, so I booked an appointment a month in advance.

If you have any concerning symptoms, it might be a good idea to call early.

Other hospitals have described my cat as unruly and restless, but here she wasn't unruly at all, and the doctor was very gentle.

I'll be going back for more detailed tests, and I hope everything is okay.

I was impressed that the medication instructions were clearly printed on the back; I've never encountered a clinic that did that before.

I hope all cats get better soon.

I went there because it was a cat-only hospital. The doctor was very nice and willing to listen to my concerns and treat my cat kindly, but they don't take reservations, so unless you're first in line, you have to wait a long time, and the place is overflowing with pet owners who don't come alone. I wish they wouldn't be in the waiting room with me. They even sit there... Despite claiming to be a cat-only hospital, they have no consideration for cats, and my beloved cat is extremely stressed. It's unfortunate, but I stopped going there because of the stress and burden it was causing my cat.
The kind and courteous service made me feel at ease about going to the hospital.
They are kind and attentive, but perhaps because they've become too famous, there are often many patients, and you may have to wait a long time.
The doctor is very kind, so my cat doesn't hiss or get scared during examinations. 😺 However, sometimes she does hiss as a greeting. 😸 …

The service was mechanical and impersonal, lacking any sense of compassion. I was even forced to undergo unnecessary surgery. Everything about it left a bad impression, so I haven't gone back since. Later, I went to another hospital with …

This is an excellent hospital and doctor. Two years ago, my elderly cat suddenly lost weight. The nearest veterinary clinic said the cause was unknown, but when we took him here, it was diagnosed as lymphoma. After about a year of …
